findings.evidence: The canonical sitemap cohort is checked against generated HTML; priority bias and context pages must retain observed inbound crawlable links, and continuation targets must resolve directly to canonical sitemap URLs rather than aliases or redirects.

New continuation cards use explicit job labels and descriptive destination titles. The deterministic gate rejects empty or generic click-here/read-more/article labels inside the new controlled continuation surface without pretending that every legacy anchor must use exact-match keywords.

The final-artifact gate constructs inbound and main-content inbound graphs across the canonical sitemap cohort. Canonical bias and context pages must have both inbound and contextual discovery; no synthetic authority score or universal click-depth rule is emitted.

Existing relations-v2 reviewed edges remain reciprocal, context-to-bias links already have generated bias-to-context reverse paths, and comparison/context data now feeds the new continuation layer so semantic relationships are reused rather than replaced by random related-content rails.

Canonical bias pages now expose a visible Home → Explore biases → category path while their BreadcrumbList converges on Home → Explore biases → canonical bias. Context, comparison and research families receive visible user-path breadcrumbs without inventing category URLs that do not exist.

A compact Continue from here block is generated only when curated evidence, context, comparison or reviewed relation data provides a specific next step. Unreviewed pages are not given a generic sitewide block merely to increase internal-link counts; their existing related-entry surface remains the fallback.

Canonical bias pages and selected context/comparison/research pages receive a compact Save, Share, Copy link and Cite utility bar. Web Share progressively enhances with canonical copy fallback, and Save uses browser-local storage with no account or server-side persistence claim.

Copy, Share and Cite derive the destination from the page canonical link. The citation is intentionally lightweight and uses the visible title plus Cognitive Biases publisher identity; it does not invent authors, review dates, DOI identifiers or academic publication status.

No prominent Google Preferred Sources control is published in this rollout because site availability in Google's source-preferences tool has not been verified. The feature remains an optional audience-distribution affordance rather than a ranking requirement.

Build-time checks verify priority inbound/contextual paths, canonical continuation targets, utility contracts, BreadcrumbList convergence and reciprocal reviewed relations. A bounded post-deploy live check verifies representative published pages without converting sample coverage into whole-site outcome evidence.
